sources.name: Google Play Console Help: Requirements for distributing apps in Korea
sources.factual_use: Google explains that access to content designated harmful to juveniles in Korea can require both age and real-name verification, and that users may need to verify that they are 19 or older.

sources.name: NAVER Help: Why legal name and age verification is required
sources.factual_use: NAVER lists paid or purchasing services, NAVER Game, and adult digital content as services that may require legal-name or age verification.

sources.name: NAVER Help: Legal-name verification for overseas residents
sources.factual_use: NAVER documents mobile or i-PIN verification, a separate customer-center document route for people residing overseas, name/date-of-birth matching, masking rules, service restrictions, and processing delay.

sources.name: NAVER Help: Foreign Passport Verification
sources.factual_use: Foreign nationals can use an eligible unexpired non-Korean passport for supported reservation or ordering services; the passport name and birth date must match the NAVER account and a live face check is used.

sources.name: KT official PASS phone-number login guide
sources.factual_use: KT describes PASS as a free mobile identity-verification method, explains the push/PIN or biometric flow, and says eligible foreign mobile subscribers who can use phone identity verification may use it.

sources.name: KISA Identity Verification Support Portal: mobile phone verification
sources.factual_use: KISA distinguishes SMS mobile verification from the PASS app flow and shows that both start from information tied to the user's mobile phone.

sources.name: Korean National Law Information Center: Juvenile Protection Act revision history
sources.factual_use: Official legal source used to cross-check that Korean youth-protection rules include age and identity checks; the article relies on the platform help pages for the user-facing procedure.

notes: Content rating, age confirmation, and legal identity verification are different gates; passing one does not guarantee the others.
A short-stay tourist SIM that is not registered for Korean mobile identity verification is not equivalent to a resident's own-name Korean mobile line.
NAVER's foreign-passport route is explicitly described for supported reservation and ordering services and must not be generalized to all NAVER adult content or all Korean apps.
NAVER's manual document route is described for people residing outside Korea; visitors currently in Korea should follow the service-specific help path rather than assuming eligibility.
KT says PASS itself is free, but the user still needs an eligible mobile subscription and data or SMS access; carrier and plan costs are separate.
Name, birth date, gender marker, nationality, residence-card data, and mobile subscriber record may need to match exactly; Romanization and spacing differences can cause failures.
The article does not recommend using another person's phone, identity, residence number, or account because that defeats the verification purpose and can create account and payment problems.
Verification is not a purchase cancellation or refund mechanism; paid-content refunds remain controlled by the store or app's purchase rules.
Community text, unopened search URLs, and suggestions were not used as factual evidence or as proof of demand.

topic_context.difference_from_existing: No live Korea Easy Guide post explains the separate Korean app gates for content rating, legal-name verification, carrier/PASS verification, and limited foreign-passport alternatives. Existing SIM, mobile-payment, NAVER Reservation, and long-stay guides cover adjacent setup tasks but not this failure path.

research_method: Opened and read current Google Play, NAVER, KT, KISA, and Korean legal pages before writing. No search-result URL was counted as factual evidence.
